architecture.mechanism: Event-driven remote assistance as a fallback layer — when the automated system leaves its nominal operational state, tasks are divided between the vehicle and a remote human operator whose cognitive reasoning resolves the off-nominal situation.
architecture.intervention: Add an event-driven fallback to the Camry automated stop system: continuously verify the parked state (gear position, wheel speed, inclinometer) and, if motion begins while Park is commanded on a flat surface, immediately command the electronic parking brake to hold the vehicle while escalating an alert to a remote operator/owner app for cognitive verification and confirmation of the secure state.
architecture.expected_effect: Any unintended rollaway is caught as an off-nominal event and corrected by the fallback (automated brake application plus remote human verification), so the vehicle remains stationary when parked on a flat surface with occupants exited.
architecture.falsification_test: Place the vehicle on a flat surface in Park with occupants exited, simulate a park-mechanism disengagement, and verify the system detects motion within a fixed threshold (e.g., <0.5 s and <0.3 m travel), applies the electronic parking brake to a full stop, and logs the remote escalation; repeat across many trials confirming zero rollaways beyond threshold and no false triggers during normal park cycles.
